semantics: partial materialization (master brief §16/§37/§66): View::Rect and View::Tile partial views over a parsed stream (src/partial.rs). A partial decode is a demand plan (backward from the requested region: frame t-1 must be exact only where frame t's COPY_RECT/MOVE_RECT ops read it) followed by a forward replay that paints each level only inside its demanded region - decode work tracks the region of interest, never the canvas. Canvas ops read only the previous frame and overpaint the fresh base, so every demanded position's value is exactly the whole-frame value (base paint, last-covering copy source, or residual). View::FullFrame (and any full-canvas box) replays the canonical step machinery (materialize_full + step_frame): byte- and error-identical with whole-frame decode by construction. Sub-frame views validate everything that contributes to the region (state transitions, op framing, whole residual containers incl. full point-list validation and kind-2 DC/AC stream decode) and paint only demanded samples; content that never contributes is not audited (documented sampling contract: a view is exact on its samples, whole-frame decode remains the canonical audit). Demand regions are merged per-row spans saturating to the whole canvas beyond a span budget (sound over-approximation, bounded memory). PartialStats reports painted sample writes (base/copy/residual), levels materialized, frames replayed, distinct objects touched, peak per-level raster memory, demand bookkeeping. Decoder::materialize_view and materialize::materialize(View::Rect/Tile) expose it.

courts.viewport_tracking_1920x1080_41f: one 200x100 textured sprite gliding 4px/frame over a static 600x900 decoration (full-HD canvas). A 260x140 tracking viewport: per decode exactly one level paints 56,400 samples (260x140 background + 200x100 sprite overpaint) vs a whole-frame level's >= 2,073,600 samples; measured release: random access to frame 40 = 0.068 ms viewport vs 13.5 ms whole (198x), all-41 viewport frames 3.4 ms total painting 2.3124M samples = 2.72% of the 85.0M-sample whole-frame lane; objects touched = 1 (the sprite; the 600x900 decoration never intersects the viewport - the decode-time analogue of object fetches); peak working raster 36,400 samples = 1.755% of the full frame; every view byte-equal to the whole-frame crop
courts.copy_chain_region: 13-frame scroll chain: a 24-wide band CopyRect-panned one pixel per interval (each level reads the previous frame) with a moving sprite; a 20x56 viewport inside the panned band: cross-frame demand propagates backward level by level and stays near the region (102,544 painted samples total over the 13 view decodes, < 13 x 15,360); every view byte-equal to the whole-frame crop - exact under real cross-frame dependency chains
courts.tile_grid_partition: a 24x24 tile grid over a 96x96 palette/index frame 8 partitions the frame exactly (16 tiles, sum of tile areas == canvas area, each tile byte-equal to the whole-frame crop); tiles are demand-planned partial decodes
courts.random_movies_parity: 12 deterministic random-content movies (random canvas 24..80, fill/raster/index/generator objects, absolute motion, palette patches, sparse overlay, copy/move rects, strict-sorted RAW residuals) x every frame x 4 random views each + FullFrame view: sample-for-sample equality with the whole-frame crop everywhere; FullFrame view == canonical whole-frame decode
courts.decoder_api_parity: Decoder::materialize_view == Decoder::materialize crop on every frame for FullFrame/whole-box/Rect/Tile views; state-level materialize(View::Rect/Tile) == whole-frame state crop (frame 0)
courts.audit_scope_hostile: out-of-range palette index inside the view -> OutOfBounds identical to whole-frame decode; a view far from the poison samples clean background (documented sampling contract - content that never contributes is not audited); unsorted residual points on the timeline -> NonCanonicalEncoding identical to whole-frame decode for any view of that frame (residual containers fully validated); residual bounds validated against the canvas, never the partial frame box
courts.work_reduction_typing: out-of-range frame index / view outside canvas / zero-size view all typed; 40-interval x 6-overlapping-tiny-copy pathological stream stays exact and bounded (demand planning saturates at the span budget, exactness preserved); PartialStats internally consistent (painted == base + copy + residual; residual writes counted only inside the region)

notes: No wire-format change in Phase S: views are requests, not stream syntax; the .vole format, materializer semantics, and every existing stream are untouched (old goldens unaffected).

The demand plan is an over-approximation by design (union over all copy destinations incl. shadowed ones; residuals add no demand), which is always exact-output-safe; region span bookkeeping saturates to the whole canvas beyond the budget so hostile streams stay in the whole-frame memory class.

Partial decode replays state transitions for every level 0..=idx (same as whole-frame replay to idx); the raster-work saving is what is measured (2.72% of the whole-frame lane on the 1080p court, 198x random-access latency on the release example).
Levels with an empty demand are skipped entirely (nothing later reads them), so a pure-procedural stream's deep frame costs one region paint regardless of depth.

Synthetic authored courts only: the numbers measure decode work on authored content; no claim about natural video or a universal speedup (§72). §66 direct scanout remains a hypothesis - this phase proves correct partial materialization and measures it, which is the prerequisite.
Recorded audit boundary: sub-frame views validate what contributes to the region; whole-frame decode (and View::FullFrame) remains the canonical audit path, byte- and error-identical by construction.
